factual_claims.claim: The company's performance was affected by several main business events, developments, and market factors.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s revenue and operating results in 2025 were impacted by several business-related and operational factors.

factual_claims.claim: Operations remained under pressure due to low private consumer and business confidence, ongoing economic challenges, and inflation in core markets, particularly Finland, which constrained consumer spending and cargo flows.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: In the financial year of 2025, the Group’s operations remained under pressure from evolving consumer behaviour and adverse microeconomic trends in its core markets of Finland, Sweden, and Estonia. Consumer and business spending continued to be restrained, reflecting the combined impact of persistent inflation...

factual_claims.claim: To optimize its cost base and adapt to the environment, the group completed the sale of three vessels during the year, namely the passenger vessel Star I in April, the cargo vessel Regal Star in August, and the cargo vessel Sailor in October.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: During the financial year, the Group completed the sale of three vessels. The passenger vessel Star I was sold to Irish Continental Group plc in April, the cargo vessel Regal Star to AMS Line Shipping Co in August and the cargo vessel Sailor to Rederiaktiebolaget Eckerö in October.

factual_claims.claim: Additionally, the group maintained three vessels on charter agreements throughout the year, including the cruise ferries Romantika, Galaxy I, and Silja Europa, with the latter two having their charters extended toward the end of the year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: As at the end of the financial year of 2025, the Group had 3 vessels chartered out... The cruise ferry Romantika was chartered out in May 2025... In September 2025, the charter agreement of Galaxy I was extended until October 2026... The cruise ferry Silja Europa was chartered out... The recent charter agreement from December 2024 was extended in December 2025 until the end of January 2027.

factual_claims.claim: Capital investments totaled EUR 33.0 million, directed mainly toward maintenance, technical upgrades, and refurbishments of vessels such as the Baltic Princess and Silja Serenade, which resulted in 73 days of planned maintenance works.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group’s investments in the financial year 2025 amounted to EUR 33.0 million... Most investments were directed toward maintenance and refurbishment of the cruise ferries Baltic Princess and Silja Serenade... In the financial year 2025, the planned maintenance works totalled 73 days.

factual_claims.claim: Furthermore, the company distributed dividends of EUR 0.06 per share, totaling EUR 44.6 million alongside EUR 11.3 million in related income tax, and the Management Board intends to propose a dividend of 6 euro cents per share for 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Annual General Meeting of Shareholders held on 20 May 2025 adopted a resolution to pay a dividend of EUR 0.06 per share in 2025 in the total amount of EUR 44.6 million... In agreement with the Supervisory Board... the Management Board... intends to propose to the Annual General Meeting the payment of a dividend of 6 euro cents per share. [Context: EUR 11.3 million related income tax mentioned under cash flow impacts].

factual_claims.claim: Overall, the reporting period was characterized as challenging due to unfavourable macroeconomic conditions and economic uncertainty in the region's core markets.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The year 2025 proved to be challenging. Tallink’s results were particularly affected by economic uncertainty in our largest market, Finland... The overall unfavourable environment in the region has constrained private consumer confidence and adversely affected cargo flows.

factual_claims.claim: Despite these headwinds, internal adjustments such as vessel sales, chartering arrangements, cost management, and reduced debt and depreciation burdens enabled Tallink Grupp to achieve satisfactory results under the circumstances, maintaining stable profitability, positive net results, and a consistent commitment to shareholder returns.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Taking all these factors into account, 2025 was a difficult year with results that can be considered satisfactory under the circumstances. We have consistently reduced our debt burden and continue to treat this as one of the priorities... Tallink aims to remain a stable dividend-paying company for its shareholders.
